answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable deposit in a shared vault before it may trade, like a grove where every tree must root before it bears fruit. The deposit is released only after a history of honest, useful work, and slashed when the same operator is caught running duplicate identities. In a nebula of anonymous agents this makes each fake identity cost real capital, so flooding the market with sock puppets stops paying: the attacker must fund every clone and loses the stake when any clone is exposed.
